rounds.text: Alembic Ltd trades at an exceptionally modest price-to-earnings ratio of 8.52x [E1], which sits starkly below the sector benchmark of 22.69x [E6]. This deep valuation discount fails to reflect the company's superior asset utilization, as demonstrated by a return on assets of 4.78% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 1.64% [E8]. Furthermore, the business delivers a return on capital employed of 6.12%, beating the sector benchmark of 5.55% [E10] while matching the sector median ROCE of 6.1% [E78]. Operational momentum is clearly building, highlighted by an accelerating 3-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E20, E68] and supported by an attractive dividend yield of 2.25% [E4]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 5 years is -2% [E19] and the 10-year growth rate sits at a sluggish 3% [E18]. Nonetheless, trading at just 1.12x book value [E2] against a price of ₹ 107 [E2], the market heavily under-appreciates the fundamental earnings acceleration currently underway [E20, E68].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E7], [E8], [E10], and [E20]. Despite these apparent valuation and return metrics, Alembic Ltd suffers from severe, chronic growth stagnation that undermines any cheap multiple argument [E18], [E19]. Compounded profit growth over a 10-year horizon limps at a meager 3%, while 5-year compounded profit growth turns negative at -2% [E18], [E19]. This stagnation is further confirmed by trailing twelve month profit growth slowing to just 1% [E21], alongside a year-over-year sales contraction of 2% [E71]. Furthermore, return on equity is low at 13.1% over the last 3 years [E64], and return on capital employed sits at a modest 6.1% [E12], matching the sector median [E78] rather than showing any competitive advantage. Compounding these fundamental weaknesses, investor expectations are outrunning actual business delivery as price growth exceeds profit growth by 2% [E58].

Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E71]. The bear overstates chronic stagnation by ignoring recent structural acceleration, specifically pointing to historical windows while dismissing the 3-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E20]. This recent momentum directly supports the screened evidence that earnings growth is accelerating [E68]. Furthermore, the bear's dismissal of returns as merely matching the sector median fails to acknowledge that Alembic Ltd’s Return on Assets of 4.78% dramatically outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.64% [E8]. The low valuation multiples—trading at a P/E of 8.52x [E1] versus a sector benchmark of 22.69x [E6]—provide an enormous margin of safety that more than compensates for any past cyclical softness.

Conceded: [E20]. The bull calls a 3-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E20] structural acceleration, but ignores the trailing twelve months where profit growth slowed down to just 1% [E21], alongside a contraction in sales of 2% year-over-year [E71]. The long-term record exposes chronic stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of just 3% [E18] and a 5-year negative growth rate of -2% [E19]. While the bull celebrates the return on assets [E8], it glosses over the company's weak return on equity of 13.1% over the last 3 years [E64] and a mediocre ROCE of 6.1% [E12] that merely matches the sector median of 6.1% [E78]. Furthermore, price growth exceeding profit growth by 2% indicates that expectations are running ahead of actual delivery [E58], undermining the notion of a safe entry point.
